instructions_tutorial: Press 'space' when the bar is on the lowest peaks of the spectrum.
peak_1: Great! This peak indicates OH-group stretching, present in water and in clay minerals.
peak_2: Correct! This peak corresponds to aromatic C=C bonds and carboxylates.
peak_2_you: Aromatic? But we're analyzing ancient pottery!
peak_3: Incredible! Si—O—Si bonds (silicates): the unmistakable signature of silica in fired pottery.
peak_1_lvl2: Interesting! This peak is the asymmetric stretching of the carbonate group (CO3)2-, a sign of carbonates in the fabric.
peak_2_lvl2: Good instinct! The Al-OH bending is the signature of dioctahedral phyllosilicates, the most common clay minerals.
peak_3_lvl2: Precise! The symmetric Si-O-Si stretching confirms it: silicates again, this time in the clay.
peak_1_lvl3: Here too! The asymmetric stretching of the carbonate group gives away more carbonates in the sample.
peak_2_lvl3: Exactly! The asymmetric Si-O-Si stretching reveals the silicate component of the sample.
miss: Too bad, you missed the correct peak. Try again more carefully!
level_complete: Great work! Let's move straight on to the next sample.
victory: Congratulations! You found every spectral peak and completed the analysis!
